entries.q: What is the difference between the i-4000 and the i-6000?
entries.a: Both have 6 cylinders mounted under the floor, a rated pressure of 3000 psi (207 bar) and a flow of 30 gpm (about 114 L/min). i-4000: rated 35 tons (≈ 31.8 t), max theoretical speed about 2.3 m/min. i-6000: larger pistons, rated 45 tons (≈ 40.8 t), about 1.6 m/min. For heavy cargo and high payloads, lean towards the i-6000.
related: What does the tractor need to run the floor?

entries.a: The W Floor is leak-tight across the full length and width of the box and keeps leachate from wet waste inside the truck. Its aluminium slats are 12.7 mm thick and each one is removable with 4 bolts. It is paired with the front-mounted BRUTE drive: rated 40 tons, 3 cylinders, two-way, with no hydraulic hoses under the trailer.

entries.a: Accelerator™ runs a two-step cycle instead of three, for light cargo. According to HALLCO it unloads up to 30% faster, can be switched on the fly while unloading and needs no bigger pump. It is standard on HALLCO drives from the i-2000 upwards.

entries.q: Which floor slat should I choose?
entries.a: Each cargo suits a profile: Standard for wood, wood chips and sawdust; AG Topseal for produce and grain; Triple Ridge for dry waste, paper and scrap; NLR for compost; NLR-HD for recyclables; Tufdeck for scrap; W Floor for wet waste. Nhu Tin confirms the profile after seeing a sample.
related: What cargo can the floor carry?

entries.a: HALLCO makes a plastic floor slat to a patented design, used instead of aluminium when cargo tends to stick to the floor. Little technical information is public yet, so Nhu Tin will ask the factory and send you documents for your cargo.

entries.q: Do you have stationary systems for bunkers?
entries.a: Yes. A LIVE FLOOR® can be fixed at the bottom of a bunker, bin or container in the plant: trucks tip the material in and the floor feeds it steadily to the conveyor. It suits boiler fuel stores burning wood chips, rice husk or cashew shells.

entries.q: Which configuration for wood chips or sawdust?
entries.a: For wood, wood chips and sawdust, HALLCO suggests an i-4000 or i-6000 drive (chosen by payload) with Standard slats. The truck unloads right in the yard, even indoors, and a clean-out tarp sweeps up the last fine chips.

entries.q: What about rice husk and produce?
entries.a: For produce and grain, HALLCO suggests the i-4000 with AG Topseal slats to limit leakage and product loss. Rice husk is very light, so Nhu Tin looks at a sample and the truck before confirming the configuration.

entries.q: Can it carry cashew nut shells?
entries.a: Yes. Cashew nut shell residue is Nhu Tin's own core cargo, delivered by our dedicated fleet to industrial boilers. HALLCO has no published configuration for it, so Nhu Tin advises from real operating experience.

Yes. Coal is heavy, so the payload per trip is high: the drive needs enough force and must not exceed its rated load. HALLCO has no published configuration for coal; Nhu Tin chooses by actual payload, usually considering the i-6000.

entries.q: Which floor for waste and scrap?
entries.a: Wet waste: BRUTE 8500 + W Floor, leak-tight. Dry waste and paper: i-4000 or i-6000 with Triple Ridge. Recyclables: i-4000 with NLR-HD. Scrap: i-4000 with Tufdeck or Triple Ridge. Compost: i-4000 with NLR.

entries.q: How does it compare with a tipper?
entries.a: A moving floor unloads with the box level, so it works in low-roof warehouses, near power lines and on uneven ground. It can unload part of a load, load cargo in (with a two-way drive) and has a leak-tight option. A tipper is still the right choice for many other jobs.
related: Can the floor unload inside a covered warehouse?

entries.q: What are the benefits of a moving floor?
entries.a: The truck unloads as soon as it arrives, with no wait for a loader or raking crew, so it runs more trips. One driver unloads alone, cutting handling costs. Nhu Tin retrofits trucks you already run, so there is no new vehicle to buy. And a level box delivers to more sites with no tip-over risk.

entries.a: Four steps: 1. Survey of the chassis, box, hydraulic supply and cargo. 2. Proposal and quote with a schedule. 3. Installation to HALLCO procedures. 4. Handover, with operation and maintenance training and warranty registration with the factory within 10 days.

HALLCO Industries, Inc. is the American company that invented the moving floor and filed its first patent in 1968. It is headquartered in Tillamook, Oregon; the group has 5 member companies, locations on 4 continents and 2 manufacturing plants.
Nhu Tin Corporation has worked in bulk haulage since 2010, supplies biomass fuel made from cashew nut shell residue to industrial boilers, and is the authorized HALLCO® dealer in Vietnam.
